diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining
where $\varphi_h \in C^{\infty}_c(\mathbb{R})$ is a cutoff function supported on $[-h, h]$ with $\varphi_h(0) = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation identifies the solution v_1 of (eq: wave v_j) (and the auxiliary v_0 of (eq: wave v_0), and likewise v_1, v_2 in the pointwise method) with the cutoff-supported plane waves, by uniqueness for the wave equation. That uniqueness argument requires the plane waves to carry the homogeneous Cauchy data, i.e. \sqrt[3]{H_1}(x,0)=0 in Ω (and H_2(·,T)=\partial_t H_2(·,T)=0 in Ω). Since H(l)=\varphi_h(l)\tau^{1/2}e^{-\tau l^2/2} is supported in |l|≤h, H_1(x,0)=H(x·\theta_0+t_0-\eta_0) vanishes on \{t=0\}×Ω only if t_0-\eta_0 > r+h, and H_2(x,T)=H((\eta_0+t_0-T)-x·\theta_0) vanishes only if T-t_0-\eta_0 > r+h. The stated admissibility conditions (T>4r, t_1>2r, t_2<T-2r, |\eta_0|≤r) give only t_0-\eta_0 > r and T-t_0-\eta_0 > r, so for admissible tuples with t_1-2r < h (e.g. (t_0,\theta,\eta_0)=(t_1,\theta,r) with \Omega=B_r) the wave slabs straddle the time slices, \sqrt[3]{H_1} does not solve (eq: wave v_j) / H_2 does not solve (eq: wave v_0), the uniqueness step is used outside its hypotheses, and neither reconstruction identity is established by the given argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the admissibility conditions by the fixed cutoff width: require t_0-\eta_0 > r+h and T-t_0-\eta_0 > r+h for all reconstruction tuples (e.g. t_1 > 2r+h, t_2 < T-2r-h, feasible with T > 4r+2h). Then the wave supports miss \{t=0\} and \{t=T\} within the projection of \Omega, the identifications v_1=\sqrt[3]{H_1}, v_0=H_2 (resp. the pointwise waves) hold by uniqueness, and both formulas are proved unchanged over a correspondingly slightly smaller admissible set.
issues.overall_effect: Both reconstruction identities (eq:recoequ Radon) and (eq:recoequ pw) are not justified by the given argument on part of the advertised admissible domain; the numerical procedure inherits the same gap (its own tuples additionally violate the stated conditions, see ISSUE-003). The limiting identities do remain true, but the paper neither states nor proves the needed support conditions.
issues.title: Reconstruction-formula derivations invoke plane-wave identification without the required support margins
issues.why_classification: A one-line strengthening of the admissibility hypotheses (a margin of the fixed cutoff width h) makes the invoked uniqueness argument valid; both reconstruction formulas, their guarantees and a comparable reconstruction domain survive, so a short local repair preserves all substantive claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now, when $\tau$ is large, the product $v_0 v_1 v_2^2 \approx \tau^{\frac{3}{2}} \e^{-\tau (|x-x_0|^2 + (t-t_0)^2)}$ near the point $(x_0, t_0)$

H_1^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\\
    H_2^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) + \theta \cdot (x - x_0)),\\
    H_3^{\tau, \theta, (x_0, t_0)}(x,t) &:= H((t-t_0) - \theta^{\perp} \cdot (x - x_0)),

issues.failure_explanation: With a = t-t_0, u = \theta·(x-x_0), w = \theta^{\perp}·(x-x_0), the product is v_0 v_1 v_2^2 = H_3 H_1 H_2 = \tau^{3/2} \varphi_h(l_1)\varphi_h(l_2)\varphi_h(l_3) e^{-(\tau/2)[(a-u)^2+(a+u)^2+(a-w)^2]}, whose quadratic form 3a^2+2u^2+w^2-2aw contains the cross term -2aw and is not proportional to a^2+u^2+w^2. Thus the claimed approximation v_0v_1v_2^2 \approx \tau^{3/2}e^{-\tau(|x-x_0|^2+(t-t_0)^2)} is false (the exponent differs), Lemma (approx identity q) — stated only for isotropic Gaussians e^{-\tau|z-z_0|^2} — cannot be applied, and the correct mass is \int e^{-(\tau/2)Q}dz \cdot \tau^{3/2} = (2\pi)^{3/2}/\sqrt{4} = \sqrt{2}\,\pi^{3/2} (the matrix of Q is diag(2) ⊕ [[1,-1],[-1,3]] with determinant 4). Consequently lim_\tau \int_\Sigma f_0 \partial^{(1,2)}|_0 \Lambda(\eps_1 f_1+\eps_2 f_2) dS = 3!\sqrt{2}\,\pi^{3/2} q(x_0,t_0): the displayed identity is false as stated and its use would return \sqrt{2}\,q(x_0,t_0).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the normalizing constant for the actual anisotropic Gaussian (total mass (2\pi)^{3/2}/\sqrt{4} = \sqrt{2}\,\pi^{3/2}) and replace 3!\pi^{3/2} by 3!\sqrt{2}\,\pi^{3/2} in (eq:recoequ pw), correcting the accompanying approximation claim accordingly (equivalently, rescale one of the waves); no other part of the argument or method changes.
issues.overall_effect: The labelled pointwise reconstruction identity is false as written: it systematically overestimates q(x_0,t_0) by the factor \sqrt{2}. The pointwise comparison method (Remark and figures) inherits the wrong scale, while its qualitative recovery and convergence rate survive.
issues.title: Pointwise reconstruction formula has wrong normalizing constant (off by factor √2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short, local recomputation of a Gaussian normalizing constant (complete the square), with no new lemma or construction; the pointwise recovery guarantee and its convergence rate survive unchanged, so only a constant is corrected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We define the admissible reconstruction domain by setting $T>4r$, $t_1>2r$, $t_2<T-2r$, and defining
For the numerical solution of the forward problem we use the parameters $N_{x_1} = N_{x_2} = 80$ and $N_t = 1500$ in the space domain $\Omega = [-0.5, 0.5]^2$ and time domain $[0, T] = [0, 3]$.
and $P$ corresponds to the interval $[-0.4, 0.4]$ divided into $63$ equally spaced distances from the origin.

issues.failure_explanation: Section 3.3 claims that, for each \eta_0 in P, setting the auxiliary wave per the tuple (T/2+\eta_0,\theta_0,\eta_0) reconstructs \radonR(q)^{rec}(\theta_0,\eta_0), i.e. it applies the identity (eq:recoequ Radon) at those tuples. The identity is only established for tuples in W_Radon = [t_1,t_2]\times\S^{n-1}\times[-r,r] with t_1>2r and t_2<T-2r. The deployed setup has \Omega = [-0.5,0.5]^2, so r = \sqrt{2}/2 \approx 0.7071, T = 3, hence admissible times must satisfy 2r < t_0 < T-2r, i.e. t_0 \in (1.414, 1.586); the tuples used have t_0 = 1.5+\eta_0 \in [1.1,1.9], which violates this for all but |\eta_0| \lesssim 0.086 of the 63 distances (and for tuples near \theta = 45^\circ,135^\circ with \eta_0 close to +0.4 the auxiliary wave's slab even straddles the final time slice, so the identification used in the derivation fails there). The prose thus claims reconstruction coverage that the paper's formal content does not support; the reported experiments are not invalidated by this gap.

failure_location.quote: With these choices, we can reconstruct $\radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\frac{T}{2} + \eta_0, \theta_0, \eta_0) = \radonR(q)^{\text{rec}}(\theta_0, \eta_0)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the numerical claims to tuples satisfying the (margin-corrected) admissibility conditions, or add the contained verification that the entry/exit margins t_0-\eta_0 > r+h and T-t_0-\eta_0 > r+h do hold for the concrete \Omega, \theta, T used (they hold except on a thin set of tuples near the diagonal angles at the largest distances, which must be excluded or justified); the displayed reconstructions themselves are unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The stated numerical procedure's theoretical justification does not cover most of the parameter tuples at which the sinogram is actually reconstructed; the advertised applicability of the reconstruction identity exceeds what is proved, even after any margin repair.
issues.title: Numerical sinogram reconstruction performed at tuples outside the paper's admissible domain
issues.why_classification: A local fix — verifying the support margins for the concrete domain and time horizon (which hold except on a thin set) or trimming the claimed parameter set — restores consistency while all demonstrated numerical results and guarantees survive; no new proof architecture is needed.
